page: The Amazon Web Services c8gd.large is a compute-optimized instance based on the AWS Nitro hypervisor and powered by 64-bit ARM architecture. It features an AWS Graviton ARMv9 Neoverse-V2 processor clocked at 2.8 GHz, delivering 2 dedicated physical cores without simultaneous multithreading. Memory is provisioned at 4.0 GB, establishing a 1:2 vCPU-to-RAM ratio of 2.0 GB per core. The processor includes 64 KB of L1 data cache, 2 MB of L2 cache, and 36 MB of shared L3 cache, with hardware-accelerated AES cryptography enabled. Hardware acceleration is purely CPU-driven, with zero integrated GPUs. A distinct hardware feature is the inclusion of 118 GB of bundled local NVMe SSD instance storage alongside a 1 Gbps baseline network bandwidth.

Empirical benchmark evaluation reflects solid single-threaded capabilities offset by absolute throughput constraints typical of a dual-core instance. Single-threaded efficiency is demonstrated by a Geekbench single-core score of 1815.0 and top-tier single-threaded bzip3 decompression throughput of 14.16 GB/sec, alongside a 30.31 GB/sec gzip compression score. Memory subsystems achieved 55.37 GB/sec during uncached 256 MB reads and 22.5 GB/sec for writes. Conversely, aggregate parallel throughput falls into lower benchmark percentiles due to the two-core limit, with multi-core Geekbench registering 3236.0, stress-ng multi-core achieving 3402.79, and static web serving delivering 4.96 GB/sec.

From an efficiency standpoint, the c8gd.large couples efficient Neoverse-V2 cores with bundled high-speed ephemeral NVMe storage, removing the need for external storage attachments for transient data workloads. Given its balanced 1:2 compute-to-memory footprint and fast local disk, the instance is well matched for lightweight ARM64 application hosting, containerized microservices, local caching nodes, CI/CD compilation, and batch data processing tasks with moderate concurrent execution requirements.
description: The Amazon Web Services c8gd.large is an arm64 compute-optimized instance powered by a 2.8 GHz AWS Graviton Neoverse-V2 processor on the Nitro hypervisor. Providing 2 dedicated physical cores and 4.0 GB of memory (2.0 GB per vCPU), it incorporates 118 GB of high-speed local NVMe SSD storage and a 1 Gbps baseline network interface without attached GPUs. Benchmark results demonstrate capable single-core efficiency, indicated by an 1815.0 Geekbench single-core score and 14.16 GB/sec bzip3 decompression throughput, though overall multi-threaded throughput is constrained by the two-core configuration. With its balanced compute density and integrated local solid-state storage, the instance fits lightweight ARM64 workloads including web services, CI/CD runners, caching layers, and microservices requiring fast scratch disks.
